ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Roo has 16 cards: 4 spades ( $(\boldsymbol{*}), 4$ clubs ( $*$ ), 4 diamonds ( $\bullet$ ) and 4 hearts $(\boldsymbol{v})$. He wants to place them in the square shown, so that every row and every column has exactly one card of each suit. The diagram shows how Roo started. How many of the 4 cards can be put in place of the question mark?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached image shows a 4×4 grid. The symbols already placed are: row 1 column 1 is a spade, row 1 column 3 is a question mark; row 2 column 1 is a club, row 2 column 2 is a spade; row 3 column 2 is a diamond; row 4 column 2 is a heart. Reasoning: The problem requires that each row and each column must have exactly one each of spade, club, diamond, and heart. Observing column 2, it already has row 2 spade, row 3 diamond, and row 4 heart, so row 1 column 2 must be a club. In this way, row 1 already has column 1 spade and column 2 club, therefore the remaining two empty cells in row 1, including row 1 column 3 where the question mark is located, can only place diamond or heart. So the question mark position has 2 possibilities.

method.method_draft: First read the 4-by-4 grid from the image: spade at row 1 column 1, question mark at row 1 column 3, club at row 2 column 1, spade at row 2 column 2, diamond at row 3 column 2, and heart at row 4 column 2. From the text, use the rule that every row and every column must contain exactly one of each of the four suits. Column 2 already has spade, diamond, and heart in rows 2, 3, and 4, so row 1 column 2 must be club. Then row 1 already has spade in column 1 and club in column 2, so the remaining two positions in row 1, including the question mark, must be diamond or heart. Therefore 2 of the 4 suits can go in the question-mark square.

method.method_draft: Treat each of the four suits as a separate candidate for the question mark. From the image, the question mark is in the top row, which already contains a spade at its first cell, so spade is impossible. Also from the image, column 2 contains spade, diamond, and heart below the top row; using the text rule, the top cell of column 2 must therefore be a club. Hence the top row must contain a club in column 2, so the question mark cannot be club either. The only remaining candidates are diamond and heart. Check that neither is immediately ruled out by the question mark's row or column and that each can be extended consistently, so exactly 2 suits are possible.
